neighborhoods_visited: Arches National Park / Colorado River Corridor
guide_description: One day built around the red-rock landscape that defines Moab: the sandstone fins and arches of the national park in the morning, the Colorado River canyon at midday, and the canyon-rim light show at sunset. The cluster runs north of town along US-191 and Utah-128, keeping driving to a minimum between stops.

days.cluster_tagline: Entrada sandstone, desert arches, and the river canyon that carved it all
days.neighborhood_focus: Arches National Park / Colorado River Corridor
days.neighborhood_description: The stretch of canyon country immediately north and northeast of Moab town - Arches National Park begins five kilometers from Main Street, and Utah-128 hugs the Colorado River east from the same junction. Together they cover the geological story of the Colorado Plateau in a single driveable loop.

morning.notes: The 4.8-kilometer round-trip trail gains 146 meters on slickrock with almost no shade - start no later than 7am in summer to finish before the heat becomes dangerous. The arch reveals itself only at the very end of the trail at the lip of a sandstone bowl, so resist looking at photos beforehand; the spatial surprise at the rim is the whole payoff. Timed-entry permits for Arches are required April through October and sell out weeks in advance via Recreation.gov.

afternoon.notes: The trail through Devils Garden to Landscape Arch is a flat 2.6-kilometer round trip on a graveled path - manageable in midday heat unlike Delicate Arch. Landscape Arch spans 88 meters, the longest natural arch in North America; a slab fell from the underside in 1991 and the ribbon of rock is visibly thinner on one side. The Devils Garden trailhead also has the park's only developed campground, worth noting if you plan to stay.

walk_to_next.to: Colorado River Overlook - Utah-128 viewpoint near Moab

evening.notes: A narrow mesa neck with a 300-meter vertical drop on three sides into a gooseneck of the Colorado River - the same view used in the opening of Thelma and Louise and the closing of Mission Impossible 2. Arrive 45 minutes before sunset and walk the east rim trail past the main overlook to the Shafer Canyon viewpoint, which puts the potash evaporation ponds (their vivid turquoise comes from added dye) in the foreground below the canyon walls. Separate state park entry fee applies; the park is 30 minutes from Moab town.

if_time_permits.notes: A 39-meter boulder perched on a narrow Entrada sandstone pedestal - the circumference trail is 0.5 kilometers and takes under 20 minutes. It sits directly on the main park road between the entrance and the Delicate Arch turnoff, making it a zero-detour stop on the way between morning and afternoon activities.

if_time_permits.neighborhood: Bureau of Land Management - Moab Field Office
if_time_permits.notes: A 33-meter freestanding arch on BLM land off US-191 south of Arches - no park entry fee, no timed entry, and far fewer people than anything inside the national park. The 4.8-kilometer round trip involves one short ladder and one chain-assisted slickrock section. Standing under the span puts it in better scale than any photograph - the opening is large enough to fly a helicopter through, which has actually been done.
